criteria.recorded_status: MET-L, as written ("attachment contents are never read"): the real EMLX reader (macos.EmlxMailbox) reads one byte per os.read up to the end of a line, so it cannot read ahead across a MIME boundary or past the blank line that ends a header block. Listing reads exactly the count line and the headers; reading a message reads exactly up to and including the delimiter line that ends the first text/plain part and stops, so no byte of any attachment is read (adapter-level tests instrument every os.read: a short text body followed immediately by a small attachment inside the same 4 KiB window, a header block with a payload right behind it, and an exact byte count of what was consumed). Consequence, stated: a message whose first body part is a non-text payload (an attachment, an image) before the text is unreadable (listed, counted as unreadable, not indexed) because finding the text behind it would mean reading the attachment; the owner may later decide to trade that for reading past such parts. Every mail answer carries attachments_not_searched. The attachment package (G-O18 format matrix, OCR, parser isolation) is not built, by design.
